title: fix(tree): grow skippedNodes when pooled capacity is stale
body:
## Description

`getValue` grows the backtrack stack with `append` instead of a raw reslice to `index+1`. The child descent stays outside the `wildChild` branch. The reset of the stack at entry is unchanged.

Fixes #4851

## Motivation / Bug Fixed

The pooled `skippedNodes` slice keeps the capacity captured when the context pool allocated it. `addRoute` can raise `maxSections` afterwards. The next request that needs one more backtrack frame panics with `runtime error: slice bounds out of range` inside the router, before any handler and before `Recovery`.

Confirmed sequence:
- Register `GET /a` and serve one request (pooled capacity 1).
- Register `GET /x/y/z/w`, `/x/y/:id/w`, `/x/:id/z/w` and `/:id/y/z/w`.
- Serve `POST /x/y/z/w/extra` with `HandleMethodNotAllowed`.
- Result before fix: `slice bounds out of range [:2] with capacity 1`.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Regression test added in `routes_test.go`:
- `TestLateRouteRegistrationSkippedNodes`

Ran:
```text
go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestLateRouteRegistrationSkippedNodes|TestIssue4818' .
```
PASS (1.039s).
